title: Normalized derived constant/stalk equivalence at a geometric point
statement: Let $\Omega$ be an algebraically closed field, $s=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, and $S:\operatorname{Ab}(s_{\mathrm{Et}})\to\operatorname{Ab}$ the geometric stalk at the identity geometric point [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Let $C_s:\operatorname{Ab}\to\operatorname{Ab}(s_{\mathrm{Et}})$ be the constant-sheaf functor [def-kun-constant-sheaf]. These are exact quasi-inverse additive equivalences. The canonical constant-germ maps $N\to S C_sN$ are the unit isomorphisms; the counit $C_s S G\to G$ is the unique map whose image under $S$ is the inverse of that unit at $SG$. Applying these functors termwise gives quasi-inverse equivalences $S_D:D(s_{\mathrm{Et}},\mathbf Z)\rightleftarrows D(\mathbf Z):C_s$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], preserving every cohomological lower bound. These are symmetric monoidal for ordinary derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor]: their tensor comparisons are the derived canonical germ and constant-sheaf comparisons, normalized on constant sections by $m\otimes n\mapsto m\otimes n$, and the displayed unit and counit are monoidal natural isomorphisms.
